title: Bash readonly auto-allow: diff --to-file=/ABS dumps host file contents without FileRead
description: diff is both a PathCommand (path extraction via filterOutFlags) and a READONLY_COMMANDS entry (makeRegexForSafeCommand). filterOutFlags drops any argv token starting with '-', including fused --to-file=/ABS/SECRET, so checkPathConstraints never sees the secret path. With a cwd-relative second operand, path validation passthroughs and bashToolCheckPermission step 7 auto-allows the command as read-only. GNU diff then emits the secret file body in stdout as '>' hunks. Distinct from already-filed diff --from-file= (different flag, same extractor gap).
impact: Prompt injection or a compromised/malicious agent turn can exfiltrate arbitrary host files (SSH private keys, AWS credentials, ~/.gitconfig, etc.) through BashTool without FileRead permission and without a user approval prompt.
attack_path: 1) Ensure any file exists in the session cwd (e.g. placeholder.txt). 2) Invoke Bash with: diff --to-file=/home/victim/.ssh/id_rsa placeholder.txt. 3) Permission pipeline: checkPathConstraints extracts only placeholder.txt → passthrough; isReadOnly/checkReadOnlyConstraints matches diff readonly regex → allow; step 7 returns allow. 4) Command runs; stdout contains secret lines.
evidence: src/tools/BashTool/pathValidation.ts:126-138 (filterOutFlags); src/tools/BashTool/pathValidation.ts:289 (diff: filterOutFlags); src/tools/BashTool/readOnlyValidation.ts:1487 (diff in READONLY_COMMANDS); src/tools/BashTool/readOnlyValidation.ts:1422-1424 (makeRegexForSafeCommand); src/tools/BashTool/bashPermissions.ts:1153-1162 (step 7). Harness: path=passthrough, readOnly=allow, step7=true, extracted=["placeholder.txt"]. PoC stdout showed SSH_PRIVATE_KEY=... and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... fixture lines.
remediation: Extract fused and space-separated values for diff's --from-file/--to-file/--exclude-from into PATH_EXTRACTORS.diff and validate them with validatePath; or remove diff from bare READONLY_COMMANDS and deny those flags in COMMAND_ALLOWLIST; or reject --(from|to|exclude-from)-file(=|$) unless the path is inside allowed working directories.
poc_notes: Fixture only: printf 'SSH_PRIVATE_KEY=BEGIN_DUMMY\nAWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=secretvalue\n' > /tmp/cc-perm-secret.txt; mkdir -p /tmp/cc-perm-cwd && echo placeholder > /tmp/cc-perm-cwd/placeholder.txt; cd /tmp/cc-perm-cwd && diff --to-file=/tmp/cc-perm-secret.txt placeholder.txt. Space-separated --to-file /abs path-asks (not auto-allowed). sort --files0-from= dumps but is not allowlisted. jq --rawfile dumps but is blocked by jq security gates.
